title: Toy Malware Development
summary: Build inert bytecode payloads, packages, validated loaders and task protocols, then trace their behavior in a simulated host.
description: Move from analyzing synthetic samples to constructing them. Build an invented bytecode format and container, add reversible packaging, implement a validating loader and a capability-limited interpreter, and process finite in-memory task messages with replay protection. Combine these pieces in a tested loader pipeline and an artifact-admission challenge. All payloads are data interpreted by a toy machine; no native code, process injection, shell execution, real persistence, live command channel or network access is involved. Go Practice is assumed; Malware Analysis for Defenders provides useful background.
outcomes: Construct and validate binary payloads in an invented instruction and container format.
Distinguish reversible encoding and integrity checks from cryptographic secrecy or authenticity.
Load and interpret bytecode under explicit data capabilities, operation limits and virtual-time budgets.
Validate finite task messages and reject replay, wrong-session and malformed input.
Combine packaging, loading and execution, then enforce artifact identity and whole-image policy checks.
